layers.note: A small fern of rocky slopes and ledges, its fronds scattered along a creeping rhizome among the rocks.

moisture.note: Dry rock; the fronds curl in drought and open after rain.

heat_load.note: Rocky slopes, among boulders and in their shade.

elevation_m.note: 200 to 2,500 m (Flora of North America); 2,000 to 8,000 feet in Arizona's mountains (Kearney and Peebles).

shade_tolerance.note: Sun (Fern Grower's Manual) to the shade of boulders.

coldest_c.note: Across its range, coldest-month means from about 0 to 15 °C; gone below −4 °C and above 18 °C.

hard_freeze_c.note: Across its range, lows to about −17 °C borne, gone where the year's coldest night falls below about −22 °C.

warmest_c.note: Across its range, warmest-month means from about 22 to 33 °C; gone below 19 °C, where summers are too short, and above 35 °C.

degree_days_0.note: About 3,600 to 9,500 degree-days above 0 °C, none below 2,800.

degree_days_5.note: About 2,200 to 7,600 degree-days above 5 °C, none below 1,500.

moisture_index.note: A moisture index from about 0.1 to 0.6, gone by 0.05 and above 0.8.

summer_rain.note: Needs the monsoon's summer rain: from about 0.3 of the year's precipitation in summer, gone below 0.2; up to about 0.75, gone by 0.85.

provenance.notes: Authored for the Saguaro desert scene (the west bajada of Saguaro National Park's Tucson Mountain District, about 750 m, 32.25 N 111.17 W) from general knowledge of the species and the ranges, habitats and elevations in the sources read for its spec (2026-10-19). Fairy swords (Lindheimer's lip fern) grows from Arizona to New Mexico, western Texas and Mexico on rocky slopes and ledges (Flora of North America, as Cheilanthes lindheimeri; Kearney and Peebles). Each climate range brackets the climate of that range, an approximate envelope read from these descriptions, not fitted to occurrence records; every full range holds the bajada's climate (coldest month about 11 °C, warmest about 31 °C, about 7,600 degree-days above 0 °C, coldest night about −4 °C, moisture index about 0.15, about half the year's rain in summer).
